text:
maria: heads up — noticed a perf regression on /v1/embeddings-rerank (hosted). P95 token latency jumped ~2.3x in the last deploy window, and QPS for the route is down. throwing this here for quick triage :eyes:
maria: metrics snapshot: QPS 420 (was 750 at 00:00), p50 token latency 31ms -> 55ms, p95 token latency 42ms -> 98ms, median batch size 3 (was 8), kv cache hit 18% (was ~62%).
perf-bot: profiling run attached: /links/flame/1868001234 — hot path shows lots of time in fallback_kernel_execute and kv_miss_handler (stack sample: kernel_selector->dispatch_fallback->execute_kernel).
sam: oh wow KV hit down to 18% is huge. any config change to cache TTL or key format in last night rollout?
maria: not at config level. There was a canary that switched rerank model variant to model-v2-quant (higher dim), pushed at 01:12 UTC and promoted at 01:40 UTC. correlate looks strong.
jia: model-v2-quant has different KV layout (per-layer slice size changed) — runtime treats it as incompatible with existing cache entries so misses. also it's 768-dim vectors vs 512 previously which increases token compute and memory copy.
nate: median batch size drop to 3 suggests batching heuristic is seeing longer seqs and smaller packability. did the request seq length distribution change?
lucy: I pulled s3 histograms: median seq len shifted from 58 -> 127 after the model switch (probably because the new reranker embedder uses full-context concatenation).
sam: that explains batching and kv. two simultaneous effects: larger vector dim -> slower kernels and more memory pressure; kv layout change -> huge cold cache -> repeated recompute; reduced batch sizes amplify per-token overhead.
perf-bot: quick diffs: kernel selection count for route: previous 86% used fast_fused_kernel, 14% used fallback. current: 39% fast_fused, 61% fallback. average kernel exec time per token: fast_fused 0.9ms -> 0.95ms, fallback 1.8ms -> 3.6ms.
jia: fallback is much slower as expected. kernel_selector is incorrectly marking model-v2-quant incompatible with fused kernels because quant layout flag differs. we can add a compatibility shim to treat layout variants as compatible when layer-size multiple matches.
maria: proposal: 1) rollback model-v2-quant promotion to reduce impact; 2) patch kernel_selector shim (small patch) and redeploy; 3) add dashboard panels for per-model kernel usage + kv-hit per-model + per-batch-size latency breakdown. who can own 1/2/3?
sam: I can do rollback now (own).
nate: I can file the kernel_selector PR — small heuristic change, will add unit tests for layout equivalence. estimate 3-4 hrs to review and push to canary.
jia: I’ll add the per-model metrics to the perf dashboards: new panels will include PromQLs: 
```
# per-model kernel usage
sum by(model_name, kernel_name)(rate(inference_kernel_invocations_total[5m])) / sum by(model_name)(rate(inference_kernel_invocations_total[5m]))
# kv hit rate by model
sum by(model_name)(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum by(model_name)(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))
# p95 token latency by batch size
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le, batch_size)(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])))
```

lucy: add a panel for median batch size and batch size distribution too — lots of routes will be affected if seq len shifts.
maria: also want an alert: if kv_hit_rate < 40% AND p95_token_latency increase > 30% over baseline for 5m -> alert to #eng-oncall and #eng-runtime.
sam: ack. rolling back now and will post when done.
perf-bot: rollback completed at 1868001820 (automated deploy-bot).
maria: after rollback quick-check: QPS creeping back to 700, p95 token latency down to ~46ms, kv hit ~59%, median batch size 7. still slightly worse than baseline but much closer.
nate: started kernel_selector PR branch: fix is to relax exact layout check to modulo granularity and add mapping table for quant variants. will link when ready.
jia: created dash PR (adds 3 panels + alert) — will request review from ops. Dash link: /dashboards/embeddings-rerank-kpi (draft).
lucy: FYI, for long-term we should have a model-metadata registry event that publishes layout/kv-compatibility when model is onboarded so kernel_selector can be fed deterministic flags. saving future firefights.
maria: agreed — add to infra backlog. action items: sam (rollback - done), nate (kernel shim PR), jia (dash + alert PR), lucy (model-registry ticket), maria (postmortem + notify customers if SLA impacted).
maria: tagging @product for customer FYI — customers on dedicated saw transient latency bump, possible credit.
sam: :thumbsup: will follow up in #customer-impact if needed.
nate: PR opened: https://git/repo/PR/1234 — contains tests + bench results showing fallback->fused time ratio improves.
jia: dash PR opened: https://dash/review/5678 — added per-model kernel share and kv-hit panels, and p95 by batch_size.
maria: thanks all. keeping this thread open until kernel shim is in canary and dashboard/alert are live. will update timestamps in postmortem.
perf-bot: postmortem template populated: /incidents/1868001234-pm-draft — initial root cause: promoted model variant changed KV layout + vector dim causing cache churn and fallback kernel usage; secondary cause: batching heuristic sensitivity to seq len distribution.
